item.title: Hillary Clinton testifies she has no information on Epstein’s crimes and doesn’t recall meeting him
item.description: WASHINGTON — Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton told members of Congress on Thursday that she had no knowledge of Jeffrey Epstein’s or Ghislaine Maxwell’s crimes, starting off two days of depositions that will also include former President Bill Clinton.

item.title: Deadly shooting in Cuban waters highlights obsessions with counter-revolution as US pressure mounts
item.description: MIAMI — Word from the Cuban government of a deadly encounter between its troops and a boat carrying armed expatriates is casting a spotlight on Cubans living in the U.S. who still harbor aspirations of a counter-revolution 67 years after a guerrilla uprising ushered in communism.

item.title: Crowds of Chicago mourners pay respects to Jesse Jackson at start of cross-country memorial services
item.description: CHICAGO — A line of mourners streamed through a Chicago auditorium Thursday to pay final respects to the Rev. Jesse Jackson Sr. as cross-country memorial services began in the city the late civil rights leader called home.

item.title: Columbia student detained by ICE is abruptly released after Mamdani meets with Trump
item.description: NEW YORK — Federal immigration authorities arrested a Columbia University student early Thursday, triggering protests on campus along with allegations that agents had entered the university-owned residence under false pretenses.

item.description: “Under the sea, under the sea. Darling, it’s better, down where it’s wetter. Take it from me.”

item.title: GNA cuts ribbon for new auditorium
item.description: Calling the newly renovated high school auditorium an investment in “confidence, collaboration and courage,” Greater Nanticoke Area Superintendent Dr. Ronald Grevera cut the ribbon in front of the stage Thursday evening, moments before the GNA Drama Club presented the opening night performance of “A Little Mermaid.”

item.title: Residents blast Wilkes-Barre Police Department for handling of missing person’s case
item.description: WILKES-BARRE — Community members at city council’s Thursday meeting blasted the Wilkes-Barre Police Department for what they said was a lack of urgency and mishandling in the search for 15-year-old La’Niyah “LaLa” Clark, who had been missing since January.

item.title: Northwest Area Intermediate School to close at the end of school year
item.description: The Northwest Area Intermediate School will officially close at the end of the school year as part of an effort to save money for the district amid recent financial struggles.
